sections.content:
Interesting! After clicking the blue square at (56, 16), several things changed:
1. The c background changed from (1,0)-(63,63) to (0,0)-(63,63) - probably just the HUD bar changed
2. The white region at (54,6)-(57,13) split into (56,6)-(57,11) - it shrank
3. A new white region appeared at (54,16)-(57,25) - this merged the white at (56,18)-(57,23) with the area where the blue square was clicked
4. The c marker at (51,8)-(52,10) moved to (53,8)-(54,10)
5. The N marker at (53,8)-(53,10) moved to (55,8)-(55,10)
So clicking the blue square at (56, 16) seems to have:
- Expanded the white region in that area
- Pushed the markers (c and N) downward
This suggests that clicking blue squares expands the white region and pushes everything above it downward. The goal might be to expand all white regions to fill the bottom area, or to push the markers to specific positions.
Let me think about this differently. The markers (c, N, p, Y) seem to be "floating" above the white regions. When the white region expands, the markers get pushed up or down.
Actually, looking more carefully:
- Before: W at (54,6)-(57,13), c at (51,8)-(52,10), N at (53,8)-(53,10)
- After: W at (56,6)-(57,11), c at (53,8)-(54,10), N at (55,8)-(55,10)
The white region at col 6-13 shrank from rows 54-57 to rows 56-57 (and cols 6-11 instead of 6-13). The markers c and N moved DOWN from rows 51-53 to rows 53-55.
Wait, that's the opposite of what I expected. The white region shrank and the markers moved down? That doesn't make sense if clicking expands the white region.
Let me re-examine. Actually, the white region at (54,6)-(57,13) had max col 13, but after it became (56,6)-(57,11) with max col 11. So it shrank in both height and width.
But a new white region appeared at (54,16)-(57,25), which is where the blue square was clicked. Before, there was W at (56,18)-(57,23) and b at (56,16)-(57,17). After clicking, the white expanded to include the blue square's position.
So clicking a blue square:
1. Converts the blue square to white (expanding the adjacent white region)
2. Causes some other white region to shrink
3. Pushes markers associated with the shrinking region downward
This is getting complex. Let me try clicking another blue square to see the pattern.
